title: LW-DETR: A Transformer Replacement to YOLO for Real-Time Detection

problem.summary: The paper argues that transformer-based DETR detectors had not been shown to work for real-time detection, while the dominant convolutional YOLO-style solutions carry extra NMS post-processing cost that dominates latency for small models.
statements: DETR-style detectors had not been fully explored for real-time detection and it was unclear whether they could match state-of-the-art convolutional detectors.
NMS post-processing in non-DETR real-time detectors adds end-to-end latency that dominates the total latency when the model is small.
Global self-attention in a plain ViT encoder has quadratic complexity in the number of tokens, making it expensive for real-time use.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, DETR for real-time detection remains not fully explored, and it is unclear if the performance is comparable to the state-of-the-art convolutional methods.
In particular, when the model is small, the end-to-end latency is dominated by the NMS latency.
The global self-attention is computationally costly, and its time complexity is quadratic with respect to the number of tokens (patches).

background.summary: The work builds on DETR and its improvements (deformable attention, Group DETR, DINO-style pretraining), on ViTDet's interleaved window/global attention, and on the dominant convolutional real-time detectors; the claimed gap is that transformer solutions to real-time detection had been little explored.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: base end-to-end framework the method extends
relatedWork.quote: Detection Transformer (DETR) is an end-to-end detection method, with removing the necessity of many hand-crafted components, such as anchor generation [51] and non-maximum suppression (NMS) [24].

relatedWork.name: ViTDet
relatedWork.relation: source of interleaved window and global attention
relatedWork.quote: ViTDet [36] implements the pre-trained plain ViT with interleaved window and global attentions [37].

relatedWork.name: RT-DETR
relatedWork.relation: concurrent real-time DETR baseline using a CNN encoder
relatedWork.quote: Concurrent with our work, RT-DETR [45] also applies the DETR framework to construct real-time detectors with a focus on the CNN backbone forming the encoder.

relatedWork.name: YOLO-NAS / YOLOv8 / RTMDet
relatedWork.relation: dominant convolutional real-time baselines compared against
relatedWork.quote: Existing state-of-the-art real-time detectors, such as YOLO-NAS [1], YOLOv8 [29], and RTMDet [46], have been largely improved compared with the first version of YOLO [50]

evidence.quote: In this paper, we study transformer-based solutions to real-time detection that remains little explored.
The current dominant solutions are based on convolutional networks, such as the YOLO series [1, 2, 20, 29, 32, 33, 46, 59, 65].

solution.summary: LW-DETR is a light-weight detection transformer built as a plain ViT encoder, a C2f projector and a shallow 3-layer DETR decoder, made fast with interleaved window/global attention in a window-major layout and made accurate with multi-level feature aggregation, IoU-aware loss, Group DETR supervision and Objects365 pretraining.
solution.approach: Stack a plain ViT encoder with a projector and a shallow DETR decoder, aggregating multi-level encoder features and combining training-effective techniques (IA-BCE loss, Group DETR, Objects365 pretraining) with inference-efficient interleaved window and global attention.
components: plain ViT encoder with interleaved window and global self-attention
multi-level aggregation of intermediate and final encoder feature maps
window-major feature map organization to remove permutation overhead
C2f projector connecting encoder and decoder (two-scale for large/xlarge)
mixed-query selection with top-K spatial queries from the projector
IoU-aware classification loss (IA-BCE) plus GIoU and L1 box losses
Group DETR with 13 parallel weight-sharing decoders during training
two-stage Objects365 pretraining (CAEv2 MIM then supervised)

evidence.quote: The architecture is a simple stack of a ViT encoder, a projector, and a shallow DETR decoder.
We propose to aggregate the multi-level feature maps, the intermediate and final feature maps in the encoder, forming stronger encoded feature maps.
We adopt a window-major feature map organization scheme for efficient interleaved attention, which organizes the feature maps window by window.
In our implementation, we use 3 transformer decoder layers.

experiments.summary: Five LW-DETR scales (tiny to xlarge) are compared with YOLOv8, YOLO-NAS, RTMDet and concurrent works on COCO val2017 with end-to-end latency on a T4 GPU, plus cross-domain evaluation on UVO and multi-domain finetuning on Roboflow 100.

evidence.quote: achieves 42.6 mAP with 500 FPS on a T4 GPU.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach is superior over existing real-time detectors, e.g., YOLO and its variants, on COCO and other benchmark datasets.
LW-DETR-large outperforms the closely related RT-DETR-R50 by 0.8 mAP and shows faster speed (8.8 ms vs. 9.9 ms).

limitations.summary: The authors present the work as a first step limited to real-time detection, and their explanation of why Objects365 pretraining helps DETR-based detectors far more than non-end-to-end detectors is explicitly preliminary.
items: Only real-time detection is demonstrated; open-world detection and other vision tasks remain untested.
Best accuracy depends heavily on Objects365 pretraining, which gives an average 5.5 mAP gain (6.1 mAP for the tiny model).
The differing benefit of pretraining between DETR-based and non-end-to-end detectors is not yet explained.
Latency is measured only in one environment (T4 GPU, TensorRT, fp16, batch size 1).

evidence.quote: Currently, we only demonstrate the effectiveness of LW-DETR in real-time detection. This is the first step.
The above illustration is a preliminary step. We believe that more investigations are needed to figure out the underlying reasons for the difference in benefits of pretraining.
We measure the averaged inference latency in an end-to-end manner with fp16 precision and a batch size of 1 on COCO val2017 with a T4 GPU

futureDirections.direction: Extend LW-DETR from real-time detection to open-world detection and other vision tasks such as multi-person pose estimation and multi-view 3D object detection.
futureDirections.quote: Extending LW-DETR for open-world detection and applying LW-DETR to more vision tasks, such as multi-person pose estimation and multi-view 3D object detection, needs more investigation.

futureDirections.direction: Add efficient multi-scale feature fusion, token sparsification and distillation on top of the simple baseline.
futureDirections.quote: We believe that our approach potentially benefits from other designs, such as efficient multi-scale feature fusion [34], token sparsification [36,72], distillation [5,5,9,64],

futureDirections.direction: Adopt NAS, stronger data augmentation, pseudo-labeled data and knowledge distillation as exploited by previous real-time detectors.
futureDirections.quote: We expect that our approach potentially benefits from other improvements, such as neural architecture search (NAS), data augmentation, pseudo-labeled data, and knowledge distillation that are exploited by previous real-time detectors [1, 29, 46].

equations.name: IA-BCE classification loss
equations.expr: ℓ_cls = Σ_{i=1..N_pos} BCE(s_i, t_i) + Σ_{j=1..N_neg} s_j² BCE(s_j, 0)

equations.name: overall objective
equations.expr: ℓ_cls + λ_iou ℓ_iou + λ_L1 ℓ_1, with λ_iou = 2.0 and λ_L1 = 5.0

equations.name: box regression reparameterization
equations.expr: b_w = exp(δ_w) * p_w, b_h = exp(δ_h) * p_h, b_cx = δ_x * p_w + p_cx, b_cy = δ_y * p_h + p_cy

applications.detail: The paper motivates the work as real-time object detection having wide real-world applications.
applications.quote: Real-time object detection is an important problem in visual recognition and has wide real-world applications.

applications.detail: Generalization is tested on Roboflow 100, which spans seven real-life imagery domains such as aerial, underwater, documents and electromagnetic.
applications.quote: RF100 consists of 100 small datasets, 7 imagery domains, 224k images, and 829 class labels. It can help researchers test the model’s generalizability with real-life data.

deploymentClaims: LW-DETR-tiny reaches 42.6 mAP at 500 FPS on a T4 GPU (fp16, batch size 1, TensorRT-8.6.1).
End-to-end latency is measured on COCO val2017 with a T4 GPU using TensorRT-8.6.1, CUDA-11.6 and cuDNN-8.7.0.
Being a DETR, LW-DETR needs no NMS, so its total latency equals the model latency.

evidence.quote: Our LW-DETR does not need NMS and the total latency is equal to the model latency.
The efficientNMSPlugin in TensorRT is adopted for efficient NMS implementation.
